name: Modimelanotide
lead: Modimelanotide (AP-214, ABT-719, ZP-1480) is a peptide drug derived from alpha-MSH, the hormone that drives skin and hair pigmentation. It belongs to the same melanocortin family as afamelanotide and Melanotan II, which people discuss for pigmentation and tanning.[1][2]
It was developed by Action Pharma, Abbott, AbbVie and Zealand and studied for acute kidney injury, where it did not succeed in clinical trials and development stopped.[1]

chain: MC1 activation is the pigmentation pathway
Skin and hair pigmentation in the alpha-MSH family
angle.text: Modimelanotide is an alpha-MSH analog, and MC1 activation by this family drives pigmentation. Its own development targeted kidney injury, not tanning.

paras: It is a non-selective melanocortin receptor agonist, with reported IC50 values of 2.9 nM at MC1, 1.9 nM at MC3, 3.7 nM at MC4 and 110 nM at MC5.[1] Alpha-MSH itself is a 13-amino-acid peptide cleaved from ACTH, and MC1 activation drives its pigmentation effect.[2]
The compound was studied for acute kidney injury, showing efficacy in animal models but failing in clinical trials.[1]
No studies found for appearance or pigmentation uses. Kidney injury trials are the only human studies reported, and they did not succeed.[1]

card.summary: Alpha-MSH analog in the pigmentation-pathway peptide family, developed for kidney injury.

quick.overview:
Modimelanotide is a melanocortin peptide derived from alpha-MSH, the hormone behind skin and hair pigment.

It was developed for acute kidney injury rather than tanning, and development stopped after trials failed.
quick.mechanism: It activates several melanocortin receptors (MC1, MC3, MC4, MC5). MC1 is the pigmentation receptor.
quick.risks: It is investigational and not an approved product, and its development was abandoned.
